blocks.body: TC-03 built a resistor, a capacitor, an inductor, a fuse, a switch, a diode, and a transistor model. This bench adds the parts that lab left out, then asks you to point at them on the official figures.

parts.name: Potentiometer
parts.behavior: A variable resistor. Turning it changes resistance, which is why it can be a volume control. It is still a resistor.

parts.name: Battery chemistry
parts.behavior: A nickel-metal hydride or lithium-ion cell in this course is rechargeable. A carbon-zinc cell is not. The symbol is still a battery either way.

parts.name: Diode
parts.behavior: Current passes one way, from anode to cathode. The cathode lead is often marked with a band. There is a small forward voltage drop when it conducts.

parts.name: LED
parts.behavior: A light-emitting diode. It emits light when current flows through it in the conducting direction. The electrodes are still anode and cathode.

parts.name: Bipolar transistor
parts.behavior: Three regions, and three electrodes: emitter, base, and collector. A small change at the base can control a larger current. That ratio is gain. It can also act as a switch.

parts.name: FET
parts.behavior: Field-effect transistor. The electrodes are source, gate, and drain. The gate controls the current from source to drain.

parts.name: SPDT switch
parts.behavior: Single pole, double throw: one common contact connects to either of two other contacts. An SPST switch is simpler: it only opens or closes one path.

blocks.body: The pictures are the NCVEC figures for this pool, stored from the official download. A schematic uses standard symbols for the electrical jobs. It does not draw the photograph of the part.

figures.ask: Figure T-1, part 1. The zigzag in the line is which part?

choices.label: Resistor
choices.why: The zigzag is the resistor. It opposes current.

choices.label: Battery
choices.why: The battery is the stack of unequal lines, part 4 on this figure.

figures.ask: Figure T-1, part 2. The circle with the arrow is which part?

choices.label: Transistor
choices.why: That symbol is the transistor. In this circuit it can control the lamp current.

choices.label: Fuse
choices.why: A fuse is not drawn as a circle with an arrow.

figures.ask: Figure T-1, part 4. The stacked unequal lines are which part?

choices.label: Battery
choices.why: Those lines are the battery, the source in this little circuit.

choices.label: Antenna
choices.why: The antenna is a triangle on Figure T-3, not this stack.

figures.ask: Figure T-2, part 3. The simple break in the line is which switch?

choices.label: A single on-off switch
choices.why: It opens or closes one path. An SPDT switch would offer two throws.

choices.label: A transformer
choices.why: The transformer is the pair of coils, part 4.

figures.ask: Figure T-2, part 4. Two coils side by side are which part?

choices.label: Transformer
choices.why: The transformer couples the incoming side to a different AC voltage.

choices.label: Resistor
choices.why: Resistors are the zigzags, parts 2, 7, and 9.

figures.ask: Figure T-2, part 8. The diode with the small arrows is which part?

choices.label: LED
choices.why: The arrows mark a light-emitting diode. Part 5 is a rectifier diode without those arrows. Part 10 is a Zener diode.

choices.label: Capacitor
choices.why: The capacitor is the two plates, part 6.

figures.ask: Figure T-2, part 9. The zigzag with an arrow is which part?

choices.label: Potentiometer
choices.why: The arrow means the resistance is variable.

choices.label: Fixed resistor
choices.why: A fixed resistor has no arrow. Part 7 is a fixed resistor in series with the LED.

figures.ask: Figure T-3, part 3. The coil with an arrow is which part?

choices.label: Variable inductor
choices.why: A coil is an inductor. The arrow means it is adjustable. With the capacitors it forms a resonant circuit.

choices.label: Antenna
choices.why: The antenna is the triangle, part 4.

figures.ask: Figure T-3, part 4. The triangle at the top is which part?

choices.label: Antenna
choices.why: That symbol is the antenna.

choices.label: Ground
choices.why: Ground is the set of lines at the bottom of the coil.

blocks.body: Order a small supply, then diagnose solder joints from the picture. A rectifier changes AC into pulses of one direction. A regulator holds the voltage down to a steadier value. Shielded wire keeps unwanted signals out of the inner conductor. A meter that shows digits is a numeric display. An LED is a common visual indicator. An integrated circuit packs many parts into one package. A resonant circuit pairs an inductor with a capacitor. Rosin-core solder belongs on radio work. Acid-core solder does not. An ohmmeter on a large discharged capacitor starts near a short and then the reading rises as the capacitor charges from the meter.

joints.look: The solder is smooth, shiny, and flows onto both the lead and the pad.

choices.label: A sound joint
choices.why: The solder wetted both parts. That is the joint you want.

choices.label: A cold joint
choices.why: A cold joint looks dull and grainy, as if the solder sat on the pad instead of joining it.

joints.look: The blob is dull and grainy. It sits on the pad and the lead still looks separate.

choices.label: A cold joint
choices.why: Dull and grainy, without wetting, is a cold joint. It can look attached and still be a bad connection.

choices.label: The preferred radio joint
choices.why: The preferred joint is smooth and wets both metals.

joints.look: Only a speck of solder touches the lead. Most of the pad is bare.
joints.picture: Too little solder to bridge the lead to the pad.

choices.label: Too little solder
choices.why: The metals are not joined by enough solder.

choices.label: A bridge of excess solder
choices.why: Excess solder floods across pads. This joint has too little.

joints.look: A mound of solder reaches the neighboring pad.

choices.label: Too much solder
choices.why: The mound connects pads that should stay separate.

choices.label: A cold joint only
choices.why: The problem in this picture is the bridge, even before you judge the surface.

joints.picture: Wrong material for a radio board.

choices.label: Do not use it on radio circuits
choices.why: Acid-core solder is for other trades. It corrodes electronics. Radio work uses a rosin-type core.

choices.label: It is the best choice for a circuit board
choices.why: The acid is the problem, not a feature.

blocks.prompt: Why can you recognize a part on a schematic you have never built, if you know the symbol's job?
blocks.reference: The symbol is the job, not the photograph. A zigzag opposes current whether the part is large or small. A diode symbol marks one-way current. Once those jobs are familiar, Figure T-1 and Figure T-2 are readable even though the drawing is not a picture of the equipment.

blocks.body: Radio Lab practice. The figures stay on the official images. These questions use what you did with them.

questions.stem: What did the potentiometer do on the bench?
choices: It stored energy in a magnetic field
questions.why: A potentiometer is an adjustable resistor. Turning it changes resistance. That is why it can be a volume control.

questions.stem: Which electrodes did the diode use, and which way did current go?
questions.why: A diode has an anode and a cathode and conducts one way. The FET has source, gate, and drain. The bipolar transistor has emitter, base, and collector.

questions.stem: What did this lab mean by gain in the transistor?
choices: A small control change affects a larger current
questions.why: Gain is that control. The transistor can amplify, and it can also switch.

questions.stem: On official Figure T-1, the zigzag you named was which part?
questions.why: The zigzag is the resistor. The battery is the stacked lines. The antenna is on Figure T-3.

questions.stem: Which order did the supply path use?
choices: Load, then the transformer, then the LED
Regulator first, because it makes the AC
questions.why: The transformer changes the AC voltage, the rectifier makes one-direction pulses, the filter smooths them, and the regulator steadies the voltage for the load.

questions.stem: Figure T-3 put a variable inductor with capacitors. What kind of circuit is that pairing?
questions.why: An inductor combined with a capacitor is a resonant, or tuned, circuit.

questions.stem: Which joint did the lab treat as a cold joint?
choices: Dull, grainy, and sitting on the pad
A spool of rosin-core solder that was never heated
questions.why: A cold tin-lead joint looks dull and grainy. A sound joint is smooth and wets both parts. Acid-core solder is the wrong material even before the joint's shape.

questions.stem: TC-07 measured voltage across a source and current in series. What does this lab add about an ohmmeter on a large discharged capacitor?
choices: The reading can start low and then rise as the meter charges the capacitor
The ohmmeter must be used on a live power supply
The meter should be set to amperes and connected across the battery
questions.why: A discharged capacitor looks like a low resistance at first. As it charges from the ohmmeter, the reading climbs. Resistance is still measured with the circuit unpowered.

blocks.body: A small station supply is dark at the radio. The schematic order is battery, fuse, switch, regulator, radio. Use the checks before you replace a box.

joints.look: The battery measures its normal voltage. The fuse is open. The radio is dark.
joints.picture: Battery — open fuse — switch — regulator — radio.

choices.label: The open fuse is the break
choices.why: Voltage is present at the battery and stops at the open fuse. Replacing the radio would leave the open fuse in the chain.

choices.label: Replace the radio first
choices.why: The radio has not been shown to be the failed part.

joints.look: A new fuse restores the panel, but a lead on the regulator output is a dull grainy blob and the voltage at the radio wanders.
joints.picture: Cold joint on the regulator output.

choices.label: The cold joint is the remaining fault
choices.why: The fuse was the first break. The dull joint can still make a poor connection after the fuse is replaced.

choices.label: Add acid-core solder on top
choices.why: Acid-core solder does not repair a radio joint. The joint needs to be remade so it wets both metals.

blocks.body: The meter connections you already practiced have one misuse that damages the instrument. This bench is a simulation.
